pages.text: Mom used her bread paddle to set the first bread on the shelf. Steam rose. Coco lifted their nose and gulped. "The very first bite is mine!" The doorbell was still quiet.
Coco quickly grabbed the top loaf. "Me first!" Mom waved a paw in surprise. "Coco, wait!" Grandpa Mole, who bought the first bread every morning, hadn't arrived yet.
Jingle! Grandpa came in and saw the empty first plate. "Oh dear! Is today's first bread already gone?" Coco quietly hid the paw holding the bread behind their back and turned halfway away.

Instead of scolding, Grandpa sat beside Coco. "Ho ho! You must have been very hungry." Mom put fresh bread on a plate and set it before Grandpa first. Coco sneaked a look at the bread behind their back.
Grandpa held Coco's front paw. "The first bread tastes better when we wait and eat together." Mom smiled. "Every morning in our shop, we do this." She sang, "Grandpa first, then Coco!"

Mom explained the rule. "One, first bread on a plate! Two, in front of Grandpa! Three, once he takes a bite, eat together!" Coco nodded and held their paws neatly together. The hidden bread went gently onto a plate too.
Grandpa broke the bread in half and took a bite. "Now you, Coco." Only then did Coco take a bite. Crisp outside, fluffy inside! "Grandpa first, then Coco!" Coco said while chewing.
The bread was the same as before, but it tasted different. "With Grandpa, it's twice as tasty!" Coco pulled the headscarf knot tight with both paws. Grandpa laughed heartily.
Coco remembered, "One, on a plate! Two, in front of Grandpa! Three, together!" The next day, before the bell rang, Coco set a plate at Grandpa's place, humming, "Grandpa first, then Coco!"
Grandpa sat Coco on his lap and hugged them. "You know how to wait. Ho ho!" The first bread tastes best when you wait and share it. Coco called from Grandpa's arms, "Grandpa first, then Coco!"
